subject: [PATCH] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock

reviews.author: Filipe Manana
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that taking the inode's rwsem in shared mode during reflink may not provide significant benefits if only a portion of the file is being reflinked and direct IO reads occur on a different range, requesting clarification in the change log.

Filipe Manana noted that direct IO reads and writes increment the i_dio_count by calling inode_dio_begin(), which may lead to issues, and suggested this as a valid concern
reviews.raw_body:
You mean a direct IO read operation happening in parallel with a
reflink using the same file as a source right?
And reflinking the entire file?

Because we only take the VFS lock (rwsem in struct inode) for direct IO reads.

However during reads (both direct IO and buffered) we always lock the
extent range in the inode's extent io tree, and the reflink also locks
the range.
So taking the rwsem in shared mode won't help much unless we are not
reflinking the whole file and direct IO reads happen on a different
range.
I think that should be explicit in the change log.

---

There is also an issue pointed out by sashiko that seems valid to me:

https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/65fa79581e1d29d6d6fabae71d23e741bff0ddf9.1788974902.git.boris%40bur.io

As every direct IO read and write increment i_dio_count with a call to
inode_dio_begin() in iomap.

Thanks.

reviews.author: Boris Burkov (author)
reviews.summary:
The author acknowledged a concern about the test cases being too implicit and promised to make them more explicit in future versions.

Author acknowledged a critical flaw in their original approach, admitted to missing a key detail, and plans to retry the patch with a revised implementation.
sentiment_signals: admitted to missing a key detail
reviews.raw_body:
I will make the test cases much more explicit in future versions of this
work, if something else comes together that makes sense in light of the
bug below.

---

Unfortunately, I think this bug is fully disqualifying for this
exact approach. I didn't notice that (or test it, clearly..)

I started this line of reasoning with pre-flushing the src outside the
lock, then found I wanted to downgrade the lock for the extent writing
after the prep stuff, then had the "insight" that just downgrading would
have the same effect but missed this detail. So I will try again with
the pre-flush + smaller scoped downgrade.

reviews.author: Boris Burkov (author)
reviews.summary: Author Boris Burkov responded to feedback from Filipe Manana, acknowledging that the patch's approach may be unnecessary due to a prior change (5d6f0e9890ed) that already avoids locking the source extent range during reflink. He asked if he was missing something else.
reviews.raw_body:
I believe that as of your patch
5d6f0e9890ed ("btrfs: stop locking the source extent range during reflink")
we don't lock the src extent range, so dio reads of the src should not
contend with reflink on that. I only see btrfs_clone_files() locking
the dst inode range by inspection as well. Am I missing something else?

2026-09-10.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Btrfs file system to downgrade the lock on the source inode during a reflink operation from exclusive to shared, reducing contention and improving performance. The change also adds a flag to indicate when an inode is being used as a reflink source, which allows direct I/O writes to take the VFS inode lock in shared mode instead of exclusive mode. This patch was tested with concurrent readers and writers and showed significant latency improvements.
